claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion.
AWS's AI business and its custom-silicon (chips) business each passed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
AWS reported $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest revenue growth since 2021.
AWS's AI business and chips business (including Trainium and Graviton) grew triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time, with Azure revenue growing 43% year-over-year in fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026, and its backlog was up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice this year.

Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year, with remaining performance obligations of $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals totaling $75 billion.
Hybrid cloud will grow from $130B to $310–330B by 2030 according to ResearchAndMarkets.
87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds, per Mordor Intelligence.
Gartner predicts 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure.
Gartner forecasts total worldwide AI spending to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Pulumi Policies can help teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates using AI.
Gartner predicts that by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms, with total spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
According to Gartner, by 2026 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% run a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said that cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are standardizing on CNCF projects, and that organizations are extending those platforms to support AI workloads.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.

In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 82% agree AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months; 63% say they trust agents to make production changes; teams expecting agents to generate half or more of infrastructure code rise from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi's report describes the gap between trust and manual approval as stated trust outrunning real guardrails, and manual approval remains close to universal today.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails in place.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%, with 30% of backend developers using Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, a decline the report attributes to growing maturity.
According to Gartner, by 2028 75% of enterprise software engineers will use AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use them.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit.
Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
Pulumi Agent Skills teach tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects.
McKinsey reports EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030 for high-performing organizations, and cloud value from innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings.
Post updated 2026-09-15 with title referencing 2027 trends.
